objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3 sqlite3;
objects.description: Opaque database connection handle used throughout the SQLite C API. Constructed by sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2(); destroyed by sqlite3_close() / sqlite3_close_v2().
VFS open file handle. Implementations may subclass by appending fields. pMethods points to sqlite3_io_methods that implement I/O on the file.
Virtual method table describing file I/O operations used by VFS implementations for sqlite3_file handles.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_mutex sqlite3_mutex;
objects.description: Opaque mutex object used by SQLite core and optionally by applications via mutex APIs.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_api_routines sqlite3_api_routines;
objects.description: Opaque table of function pointers provided to loadable extensions to call back into SQLite. Defined fully in sqlite3ext.h.

objects.definition: typedef const char *sqlite3_filename;
objects.description: Type alias for filename pointers passed to VFS xOpen and related helper APIs.
Virtual File System object defining OS interface for SQLite. Register via sqlite3_vfs_register. Fields/methods versioned via iVersion.
Pluggable memory allocator methods used with sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_MALLOC/GETMALLOC).

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_stmt sqlite3_stmt;
objects.description: Opaque prepared statement handle produced by sqlite3_prepare_* and finalized by sqlite3_finalize().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_value sqlite3_value;
objects.description: Dynamically typed value object used for SQL parameters, column results, and function arguments. Managed by SQLite; some APIs return protected/unprotected instances.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_context sqlite3_context;
objects.description: SQL function context passed to application-defined SQL scalar/aggregate/window functions to set results, access aux data, etc.
Base instance object for a virtual table. Implementations extend this struct. pModule points to module methods; zErrMsg used to report errors.
Structure passed to a virtual table xBestIndex method describing constraints/orderings and for returning chosen plan details.
Base cursor object for virtual tables. Implementations extend this struct to carry scan state.
Method table for a virtual table module. Register with sqlite3_create_module[_v2].

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_blob sqlite3_blob;
objects.description: Opaque handle for incremental BLOB I/O opened by sqlite3_blob_open() and closed by sqlite3_blob_close().

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_pcache sqlite3_pcache;
objects.description: Opaque page-cache object used by custom pcache implementations.
Single page record handed to/managed by custom pcache implementations. pBuf points to page content; pExtra to caller-defined metadata.
Pluggable page cache method table set via sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2/GETPCACHE2).
Deprecated/legacy page cache methods structure (pre-3.6). Prefer sqlite3_pcache_methods2.

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_backup sqlite3_backup;
objects.description: Opaque handle for online backup operation created by sqlite3_backup_init() and finished by sqlite3_backup_finish().
Custom mutex implementation methods set via sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_MUTEX/GETMUTEX).

objects.definition: typedef struct sqlite3_str sqlite3_str;
objects.description: Opaque dynamic string builder created by sqlite3_str_new() and finalized by sqlite3_str_finish()/sqlite3_str_free().
Opaque object capturing a WAL database snapshot for opening historical read transactions via sqlite3_snapshot_open(). Created by sqlite3_snapshot_get() and freed by sqlite3_snapshot_free().
Context passed to legacy R-Tree geometry callbacks registered via sqlite3_rtree_geometry_callback(). Holds user context, parameters, and optional destructor.
Extended query context for R-Tree 2nd-gen callbacks registered by sqlite3_rtree_query_callback(). Includes geometry parameters and traversal state with scoring and within flags.
API provided to FTS5 auxiliary functions to inspect current match context, tokenize text, iterate phrase occurrences, manage auxdata, etc.

objects.definition: typedef struct Fts5Context Fts5Context;
objects.description: Opaque context passed into FTS5 extension functions representing the current FTS5 query row and environment.

objects.definition:
typedef struct Fts5PhraseIter Fts5PhraseIter;
struct Fts5PhraseIter { const unsigned char *a; const unsigned char *b; };
objects.description: Iterator state used with FTS5 API xPhraseFirst/Next methods to walk matches or matching columns.

objects.definition: typedef struct Fts5Tokenizer Fts5Tokenizer;
objects.description: Opaque tokenizer instance used by FTS5 custom tokenizers.
Structures defining FTS5 custom tokenizer method tables. v2 adds locale-aware xTokenize and version field; legacy struct retained for compatibility.
Entry-point API passed to FTS5 auxiliary and tokenizer extensions to register custom tokenizers and functions and to look them up.
Function pointer type for loadable extension entry point sqlite3_extension_init(). Used by the extension loading mechanism.

functions.name: sqlite3_libversion
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 string literal of the SQLite runtime library version (e.g., "3.52.0"). Use to verify the runtime version at execution time.
requirements: Call at any time; no database handle required.
Return is a pointer to static storage; do not free or modify.
Thread-safe to call concurrently.

functions.name: sqlite3_sourceid
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 string literal identifying the exact SQLite source check-in used to build the library (date/time and SHA hash).
requirements: Call at any time; no database handle required.
Return is static storage; do not free or modify.
Value may differ in last four hex digits if amalgamation was edited.

functions.name: sqlite3_libversion_number
functions.description: Returns the runtime library version as an integer (X*1000000 + Y*1000 + Z).
requirements: Call at any time; no handle required.
Thread-safe.

functions.name: sqlite3_compileoption_used
functions.description: Returns 1 if the named compile-time option (with or without SQLITE_ prefix) was defined when the library was built, else 0.
requirements: Argument must be a zero-terminated UTF-8 string of the option name. SQLITE_ prefix may be omitted.
May be compiled out if SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS; then always returns 0.

functions.name: sqlite3_compileoption_get
functions.description: Enumerates the compile-time options; returns the N-th option string (without SQLITE_ prefix) or NULL if N is out of range.
requirements: N must be >=0. Iteration continues until NULL.
May be compiled out if SQLITE_OMIT_COMPILEOPTION_DIAGS; then returns NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_threadsafe
functions.description: Reports the compile-time mutex setting (SQLITE_THREADSAFE) of the library. Returns 0 if compiled without mutexes, non-zero otherwise. Not affected by runtime sqlite3_config().
requirements: Can be called anytime.
Reports compile-time setting only; does not reflect runtime mode changes.

functions.name: sqlite3_close
functions.description: Destructor for a database connection. Closes the connection and frees associated resources if there are no outstanding statements/blobs/backups; otherwise leaves it open and returns SQLITE_BUSY.
requirements: Argument must be NULL or a valid sqlite3* obtained from sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2() and not previously closed.
Must finalize all prepared statements, close all blobs, finish all backups before calling to avoid SQLITE_BUSY.
Calling with NULL is a no-op.
If closed while a transaction is open, the transaction is rolled back.

functions.name: sqlite3_close
functions.description: Destructor for an open sqlite3 database connection handle. Attempts to close the database and deallocate all resources. Returns SQLITE_OK on success or SQLITE_BUSY if there are unfinalized prepared statements, open BLOB handles, or unfinished backups associated with the connection.
requirements: The argument must be either NULL (a no-op) or a valid sqlite3* obtained from sqlite3_open(), sqlite3_open16(), or sqlite3_open_v2() and not previously closed.
All prepared statements must be finalized, all BLOB handles closed, and all sqlite3_backup objects finished before calling, otherwise SQLITE_BUSY is returned and the connection remains open.
Calling with NULL is a harmless no-op.

functions.name: sqlite3_close
functions.description: Close database connection if no unfinalized statements/blobs/backups remain; otherwise returns SQLITE_BUSY and leaves connection open.
requirements: Pass NULL is no-op.
Caller must finalize/close all dependent objects first.

functions.name: sqlite3_close_v2
functions.description: Like sqlite3_close(), but if there are outstanding statements/blobs/backups it marks the connection as a zombie and defers deallocation until all are finalized/closed/finished. Always returns SQLITE_OK for valid pointer.
requirements: Argument must be NULL or a valid, not-previously-closed sqlite3* from an open() API.
Calling with NULL is a no-op.
Designed for GC’d host languages; do not reuse a zombie handle (it becomes unusable).

functions.name: sqlite3_close_v2
functions.description: Destructor variant for sqlite3 that marks the connection as a "zombie" and defers deallocation until all prepared statements, blob handles, and backups are cleaned up. Returns SQLITE_OK even if objects remain, unlike sqlite3_close, which returns SQLITE_BUSY.
requirements: The argument must be NULL or a valid, not-previously-closed sqlite3*.
If there are unfinalized statements, blobs, or backups, the connection becomes unusable and will be deallocated automatically after those are finalized/closed/finished.
Calling with NULL is a no-op.

functions.name: sqlite3_close_v2
functions.description: Close database or mark as zombie if outstanding objects exist; returns SQLITE_OK regardless and finalizes when last object is closed.
requirements: db may be NULL (no-op).

functions.name: sqlite3_exec
functions.signature: int sqlite3_exec(sqlite3* db, const char *sql, int (*callback)(void*,int,char**,char**), void *arg, char **errmsg);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that prepares, steps through, and finalizes UTF-8 SQL text possibly containing multiple semicolon-separated statements. For each row of each statement, invokes callback if non-NULL. On error, stops processing; if errmsg is not NULL, sets it to a malloc’d message to be freed by sqlite3_free().
requirements: db must be a valid, open database and must not be closed while sqlite3_exec() runs.
sql must point to read-only SQL text for the duration of the call; do not modify while running.
If callback is provided, it must not modify the database connection (not reentrant) and must not access out-of-scope row/column arrays after it returns.
If callback returns non-zero, sqlite3_exec() aborts and returns SQLITE_ABORT.
If errmsg != NULL and an error occurs, application must call sqlite3_free(*errmsg).
Do not dereference callback arrays after returning; pointers are transient.
Passing NULL, empty, or comment-only SQL text executes nothing.

functions.name: sqlite3_initialize
functions.description: Explicitly initializes the SQLite library. Normally not required (autoinit), but useful when compiled with SQLITE_OMIT_AUTOINIT or for embedded environments.
requirements: Thread-safe; can be called multiple times—only the first effective call does initialization.
Should be called before any other SQLite API if SQLITE_OMIT_AUTOINIT is used.
Returns non-OK on failure (e.g., OOM).

functions.name: sqlite3_shutdown
functions.description: Deinitializes SQLite and releases resources allocated by sqlite3_initialize(). Intended for embedded systems; workstation apps usually need not call it.
requirements: Not threadsafe: must only be called from a single thread.
All open database connections must be closed and all other SQLite resources deallocated before calling.
Only the first effective call performs shutdown; others are no-ops.

functions.name: sqlite3_os_init
functions.description: Performs OS-specific SQLite initialization (allocates static resources, sets up default VFS, etc.). Called by sqlite3_initialize().
requirements: Applications must NOT call this directly. It is for platform ports only.
If building for nonstandard platforms (SQLITE_OS_OTHER=1), application must supply this function; must return SQLITE_OK on success.

functions.name: sqlite3_os_end
functions.description: Performs OS-specific SQLite shutdown; undoes effects of sqlite3_os_init(). Called by sqlite3_shutdown().
requirements: Applications must NOT call this directly. It is for platform ports only.
If supplied by application (SQLITE_OS_OTHER=1), must return SQLITE_OK on success.
Only called after sqlite3_shutdown().

functions.name: sqlite3_config
functions.description: Global library configuration interface. Must be called before sqlite3_initialize() (or after sqlite3_shutdown()) for most options. Some options are “anytime”. Accepts varargs depending on op.
requirements: Not threadsafe. Ensure no other SQLite interfaces are running concurrently.
Most ops must be called before initialization; otherwise returns SQLITE_MISUSE unless op is an anytime option.
Check return code for unknown/unsupported ops (non-zero).
Some ops require specific pointer types or integers as documented in header; use exact types.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_config
functions.description: Per-connection configuration changes. Varargs depend on op. Returns SQLITE_OK if successful.
requirements: db must be a valid open sqlite3* handle.
Arguments must match the selected op as documented (e.g., int and int* for ENABLE_FKEY).
Some ops can only be called when the connection is not using the feature (e.g., LOOKASIDE requires not in-use, else SQLITE_BUSY).
Check return code for unsupported ops.

functions.name: sqlite3_extended_result_codes
functions.description: Enable or disable extended result codes for a database connection. When enabled, many APIs may return extended result codes instead of primary result codes.
requirements: The database connection must be valid.
onoff should be non-zero to enable, zero to disable.
Check return codes accordingly after enabling extended result codes.

functions.name: sqlite3_last_insert_rowid
functions.description: Returns the ROWID of the most recent successful INSERT into a rowid table or virtual table on the given connection. Returns 0 if none. May be affected by triggers; see docs.
requirements: The database connection must be valid.
Concurrent INSERTs on the same connection from other threads while this function runs make the return value unpredictable.
Does not record inserts into WITHOUT ROWID tables.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_last_insert_rowid
functions.description: Sets the value that sqlite3_last_insert_rowid() will return for a connection without performing an insert.
requirements: The database connection must be valid.
Intended for virtual tables or other implementations to adjust the last insert rowid value.

functions.name: sqlite3_changes
functions.description: Returns the number of database rows modified, inserted or deleted by the most recently completed INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement on the connection. Undefined if value exceeds int range.
requirements: Only changes made directly by statements are counted; side-effects from triggers or REPLACE conflict resolution are treated per docs.
Calling while another thread changes the same connection yields meaningless results.

functions.name: sqlite3_changes64
functions.description: 64-bit version of sqlite3_changes(). Returns total number of rows modified by the most recent DML on the connection.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_changes(), but safe for counts > INT_MAX.

functions.name: sqlite3_total_changes
functions.description: Returns the total number of database rows modified, inserted or deleted by all INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE statements since the connection was opened. Undefined if exceeds int range.
requirements: Only changes made by this connection are counted; changes by other connections are ignored.
Calling while another thread changes the same connection yields meaningless results.

functions.name: sqlite3_total_changes64
functions.description: 64-bit version of sqlite3_total_changes(). Returns total changes since connection opened.
requirements: Same notes as sqlite3_total_changes() apply.

functions.name: sqlite3_interrupt
functions.description: Requests interruption of any currently running operation on the database connection at the earliest opportunity. Operations will return SQLITE_INTERRUPT and in-transaction DML will cause rollback.
requirements: The connection must not be closed before sqlite3_interrupt() returns.
Safe to call from a different thread than the one executing the operation.
Has no effect if there are no running statements.

functions.name: sqlite3_is_interrupted
functions.description: Returns 1 if sqlite3_interrupt() is currently in effect for the connection, 0 otherwise.
requirements: The database connection must be valid.

functions.name: sqlite3_complete
functions.description: Checks whether the given UTF-8 SQL text forms a complete statement (ends in a semicolon not within a string/comment and not a prefix of CREATE TRIGGER). Returns 1 if complete, 0 if incomplete, or SQLITE_NOMEM on OOM.
requirements: Input must be zero-terminated UTF-8 string.
Does not parse or validate SQL beyond completeness; syntactic errors are not detected.

functions.name: sqlite3_complete16
functions.description: UTF-16 native-endian variant of sqlite3_complete(). Returns 1 if complete, 0 if incomplete, or non-zero on initialization failure.
requirements: Input must be zero-terminated UTF-16 string in native byte order.
May auto-initialize SQLite if not initialized; failure yields non-zero regardless of completeness.

functions.name: sqlite3_busy_handler
functions.description: Registers a busy-handler callback invoked when a table/database is locked. If callback returns non-zero, SQLite retries after a delay; returning 0 aborts with SQLITE_BUSY.
requirements: Only one busy handler per connection; registering a new one replaces the old one.
The busy callback must not re-enter operations that modify the same connection; it is not reentrant.
Do not close the database or statements from within the busy handler.

functions.name: sqlite3_busy_timeout
functions.description: Convenience busy handler that sleeps/retries until at least the specified milliseconds have elapsed, then returns SQLITE_BUSY. Pass <=0 to disable busy handlers.
requirements: Only one busy handler per connection; this replaces any existing handler.

functions.name: sqlite3_setlk_timeout
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_setlk_timeout(sqlite3*, int ms, int flags);
functions.description: Sets setlk (blocking lock) timeout for WAL-mode databases on VFSes that support blocking locks (SQLITE_ENABLE_SETLK_TIMEOUT builds). In non-supporting builds/VFSes, it is a no-op.
requirements: Only useful if SQLite built with SQLITE_ENABLE_SETLK_TIMEOUT and VFS supports blocking locks.
Passing 0 disables blocking locks; -1 requests indefinite blocking. Other negative values are undefined.
The SQLITE_SETLK_BLOCK_ON_CONNECT flag controls blocking on SHARED lock when connecting to WAL.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_table
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_get_table(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, char ***pazResult, int *pnRow, int *pnColumn, char **pzErrmsg);
functions.description: Legacy helper that executes one or more SQL statements and returns an entire result set as a table of strings. The array contains (N+1)*M entries, first M column names then N*M row values.
requirements: Call sqlite3_free_table() on *pazResult when finished to avoid leaks; do not pass to sqlite3_free().
db must remain open during execution; do not modify zSql while running.
Error message string (if any) must be freed with sqlite3_free().
This API is legacy and not recommended for new code.

functions.name: sqlite3_free_table
functions.description: Frees a result table obtained from sqlite3_get_table().
requirements: Argument must be a pointer previously returned via *pazResult by sqlite3_get_table(), or NULL.
Do not pass the array directly to sqlite3_free().

functions.name: sqlite3_mprintf
functions.description: printf-like string formatter that allocates the result using sqlite3_malloc64(). Caller must free with sqlite3_free(). Supports SQLite's extended formats (%q, %Q, %w, %z, etc.).
requirements: Return is NULL on OOM; caller must check and free with sqlite3_free().
Do not pass returned buffer back to SQLite APIs that keep only a transient reference unless documented.

functions.name: sqlite3_vmprintf
functions.description: va_list variant of sqlite3_mprintf(). Allocates formatted string with sqlite3_malloc64().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_mprintf().

functions.name: sqlite3_snprintf
functions.description: Like snprintf() but returns a pointer to the buffer. Always null-terminates if buffer size > 0. Uses SQLite's printf formatting extensions.
requirements: First parameter is total buffer size in bytes including terminator; a value of 0 writes nothing.
The buffer must be valid and large enough for expected output.

functions.name: sqlite3_vsnprintf
functions.signature: SQLITE_API char *sqlite3_vsnprintf(int, char*, const char*, va_list);
functions.description: va_list variant of sqlite3_snprintf().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_snprintf().

functions.name: sqlite3_malloc
functions.description: Allocates at least N bytes of memory using SQLite's allocator. Returns NULL on failure or if N<=0.
requirements: Memory must be freed with sqlite3_free().
Do not mix with system malloc/free.

functions.name: sqlite3_malloc64
functions.description: Like sqlite3_malloc() but N is a 64-bit unsigned integer.
requirements: Free with sqlite3_free().

functions.name: sqlite3_realloc
functions.description: Resizes a prior allocation from sqlite3_malloc/realloc to at least N bytes. If X is NULL behaves like malloc(N). If N<=0 behaves like free(X).
requirements: Pointer X must be NULL or a pointer previously obtained from sqlite3_malloc/realloc and not yet freed.
On failure and N>0, the original allocation is not freed.

functions.name: sqlite3_realloc64
functions.description: 64-bit size variant of sqlite3_realloc().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_realloc().

functions.name: sqlite3_free
functions.description: Frees memory obtained from sqlite3_malloc/sqlite3_realloc. Passing NULL is a no-op.
requirements: Pointer must be NULL or memory allocated by SQLite's allocator and not already freed.
Do not access memory after freeing.

functions.name: sqlite3_msize
functions.description: Returns the size of an allocation previously obtained from sqlite3_malloc()/realloc(). Returns 0 if X is NULL. Behavior is undefined if X is invalid or already freed.
requirements: Pointer must be a current SQLite allocation; do not pass arbitrary pointers.

functions.name: sqlite3_memory_used
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes of memory currently outstanding (allocated but not freed) by SQLite's memory subsystem.
requirements: Only meaningful if memstatus is enabled (default unless compiled otherwise).

functions.name: sqlite3_memory_highwater
functions.description: Returns the maximum value of sqlite3_memory_used() since the last reset. If resetFlag is non-zero, resets the high-water mark to current used value.
requirements: Memstatus must be enabled unless compile-time option disables it.

functions.name: sqlite3_randomness
functions.description: Fills buffer P with N bytes of pseudo-random data. Seeding occurs automatically from VFS xRandomness on first proper call.
requirements: P may be NULL. If N<=0 or P==NULL, seeding may occur but no bytes are written.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_authorizer
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_set_authorizer(sqlite3*, int (*xAuth)(void*,int,const char*,const char*,const char*,const char*), void *pUserData);
functions.description: Registers an authorizer callback to approve or deny specific operations during statement compilation. Callback returns SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_DENY (reject), or SQLITE_IGNORE (modify read to return NULL).
requirements: Only one authorizer per connection; setting a new one overrides any prior callback. Pass NULL to disable.
The callback must not modify the database connection (prepare/step/close).
The authorizer must be kept in place during statement preparation and potential re-prepare in sqlite3_step().

functions.name: sqlite3_trace
functions.signature: SQLITE_API SQLITE_DEPRECATED void *sqlite3_trace(sqlite3*, void (*xTrace)(void*, const char*), void*);
functions.description: Deprecated tracing API. Registers a callback invoked with the SQL statement text as execution begins (and for triggers). Use sqlite3_trace_v2() instead.
requirements: Returns prior context pointer; new registration replaces prior.
Avoid in new applications; use sqlite3_trace_v2().

functions.name: sqlite3_profile
functions.signature: SQLITE_API SQLITE_DEPRECATED void *sqlite3_profile(sqlite3*, void (*xProfile)(void*, const char*, sqlite3_uint64), void*);
functions.description: Deprecated profiling API. Callback invoked as each SQL statement finishes, with SQL text and approximate elapsed time in nanoseconds. Use sqlite3_trace_v2() with SQLITE_TRACE_PROFILE instead.
requirements: Returns prior context pointer; new registration replaces prior.
Do not use in new applications.

functions.name: sqlite3_trace_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_trace_v2(sqlite3*, unsigned uMask, int (*xCallback)(unsigned, void*, void*, void*), void *pCtx);
functions.description: Registers a unified trace callback for statement, profile, row, and close events. uMask is OR of SQLITE_TRACE_* flags. xCallback returns 0 (ignored) currently.
requirements: Only one trace callback per connection; new call overrides previous.
Do not assume reentrancy; callback should return quickly and avoid modifying the same connection in unsafe ways.

functions.name: sqlite3_progress_handler
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_progress_handler(sqlite3*, int N, int (*X)(void*), void*);
functions.description: Registers a progress callback invoked every N virtual machine instructions during prepare/step operations. Returning non-zero interrupts the operation.
requirements: Only one handler per connection; subsequent calls replace the prior.
Callback must not modify the connection (prepare/step) as it is not reentrant.
Disable by passing X==NULL or N<1.

functions.name: sqlite3_open
functions.description: Opens (and possibly creates) a database file with UTF-8 filename. Returns SQLITE_OK on success; on error, may still assign *ppDb (non-NULL) for errcode/emsg retrieval. Default mode is read/write create.
requirements: filename must be a UTF-8 string. Use ":memory:" for in-memory DB or empty string for temporary on-disk DB.
Call sqlite3_close/close_v2() to release *ppDb.
Do not assume *ppDb is NULL on failure; check return code and use sqlite3_errmsg().

functions.name: sqlite3_open
functions.description: Open or create a database file filename (UTF-8). Returns SQLITE_OK and sets *ppDb on success; on failure may set *ppDb to a zombie handle or NULL on OOM.
requirements: filename may be ":memory:" or empty string for temp db.
Caller must close with sqlite3_close/close_v2.
Use sqlite3_errmsg() for error text.

functions.name: sqlite3_open16
functions.description: UTF-16 native-endian variant of sqlite3_open().
requirements: filename must be zero-terminated UTF-16 string.
Same lifecycle and error handling as sqlite3_open().

functions.name: sqlite3_open16
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of sqlite3_open.

functions.name: sqlite3_open_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_open_v2(const char *filename, sqlite3 **ppDb, int flags, const char *zVfs);
functions.description: Opens a database with extended flags controlling read-only/read-write/create, URI handling, mutex mode, shared-cache, extended result codes, NOFOLLOW, etc. zVfs selects VFS or NULL for default.
requirements: flags must include one of READONLY, READWRITE, or READWRITE|CREATE; other optional flags as documented.
Passing disallowed flags may yield undefined behavior in some versions; avoid VFS-only flags here.
If using SQLITE_OPEN_URI, filename is interpreted as a URI with query parameters.
On success or error, follow same handle lifecycle as sqlite3_open().

functions.name: sqlite3_open_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_open_v2(const char *filename, sqlite3 **ppDb, int flags, const char *zVfs);
functions.description: Open database with flags and optional VFS. Flags include READONLY/READWRITE/CREATE, URI, NOMUTEX/FULLMUTEX, SHAREDCACHE/PRIVATECACHE, EXRESCODE, NOFOLLOW.
requirements: flags must include one of READONLY/READWRITE[/CREATE].
zVfs NULL for default VFS.
Error codes may be extended if EXRESCODE bit set.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_parameter
functions.signature: SQLITE_API const char *sqlite3_uri_parameter(sqlite3_filename z, const char *zParam);
functions.description: If F (filename) is a suitable database filename or VFS-open filename, returns the value of URI query parameter P or NULL if absent. For parameters without explicit values, returns empty string.
requirements: F must be a filename from SQLite core (xOpen or sqlite3_db_filename()) or created via sqlite3_create_filename(); passing arbitrary strings is undefined.
Returns value without the SQLITE_ prefix handling (unlike compile options).

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_parameter
functions.signature: SQLITE_API const char *sqlite3_uri_parameter(sqlite3_filename z, const char *zParam);
functions.description: Return the value for query parameter zParam from filename/URI z, or NULL if not present. The returned pointer is valid as long as the filename lifetime is valid (e.g., as passed to VFS xOpen or sqlite3_db_filename).
requirements: z must be a valid sqlite3_filename as produced by core (VFS xOpen filename, sqlite3_db_filename(), or sqlite3_create_filename()).
If z is NULL, the function returns NULL.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller; it is owned by SQLite.
Only safe to use for filenames originating from SQLite as documented; undefined behavior otherwise.

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_boolean
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_uri_boolean(sqlite3_filename z, const char *zParam, int bDefault);
functions.description: Interprets URI parameter P as a boolean: returns 1 for yes/true/on or non-zero numeric; 0 for no/false/off or numeric zero; returns bDefault if P not present or unrecognized.
requirements: F must be a suitable filename pointer as for sqlite3_uri_parameter().

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_int64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API sqlite3_int64 sqlite3_uri_int64(sqlite3_filename, const char*, sqlite3_int64);
functions.description: Returns 64-bit integer value for URI parameter P or default D if missing. Returns 0 if value is non-integer.
requirements: Filename pointer must be suitable (from SQLite core).

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_key
functions.signature: SQLITE_API const char *sqlite3_uri_key(sqlite3_filename z, int N);
functions.description: Returns the name of the N-th query parameter key for a given filename F, or NULL if out of range. N is zero-based.
requirements: F must be a suitable filename pointer as for sqlite3_uri_parameter().

functions.name: sqlite3_uri_key
functions.signature: SQLITE_API const char *sqlite3_uri_key(sqlite3_filename z, int N);
functions.description: Return the name of the N-th query parameter key in filename/URI z, or NULL if N is out of range. Indexing is zero-based.
requirements: z must be a valid sqlite3_filename obtained from SQLite as documented.
N must be >=0; if N < 0 or beyond available parameters, returns NULL.
Returned string is owned by SQLite; do not free.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_database
functions.description: Given a filename that may be a database, journal, or WAL path as seen by VFS, returns the corresponding main database filename.
requirements: F must be a filename passed by core to VFS xOpen or obtained from sqlite3_db_filename(). Passing other values is undefined.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_journal
functions.description: Returns the associated rollback journal filename for the given database/journal/WAL filename.
requirements: F must be from core/VFS as above.

functions.name: sqlite3_filename_wal
functions.description: Returns the associated WAL filename for the given database/journal/WAL filename.
requirements: F must be from core/VFS as above.

functions.name: sqlite3_database_file_object
functions.description: If X is the name of a rollback or WAL journal file passed to VFS xOpen, returns the sqlite3_file object for the corresponding main database file.
requirements: Intended for custom VFS use only. Argument must be a filename pointer from xOpen with flags indicating journal/WAL. Any other use is undefined.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_filename
functions.signature: SQLITE_API sqlite3_filename sqlite3_create_filename(const char *zDatabase, const char *zJournal, const char *zWal, int nParam, const char **azParam);
functions.description: Allocates a composite filename object bundling main DB, journal, WAL, and URI parameters for use by VFS shims. Must be freed by sqlite3_free_filename().
requirements: zDatabase, zJournal, zWal must be non-NULL (can be empty strings).
If nParam>0, azParam must be an array of 2*nParam non-NULL pointers (key/value pairs).
On OOM may return NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_free_filename
functions.description: Frees a filename object previously returned by sqlite3_create_filename().
requirements: Argument must be NULL or a pointer previously returned by sqlite3_create_filename(). Do not free while VFS still using it.

functions.name: sqlite3_errcode
functions.description: Returns the most recent error/result code for API calls on the connection.
requirements: The error code may change after subsequent API calls. Some interfaces are guaranteed not to change it (errcode/errmsg/errmsg16/error_offset/db_handle).

functions.name: sqlite3_extended_errcode
functions.description: Returns the most recent extended error code, even if extended result codes are disabled.
requirements: Same volatility caveats as sqlite3_errcode().

functions.name: sqlite3_errmsg
functions.description: Returns a UTF-8 English-language string describing the most recent error for the connection, or NULL if none.
requirements: Pointer may become invalid after subsequent SQLite calls. String is managed by SQLite; do not free.

functions.name: sqlite3_errmsg
functions.description: Return English UTF-8 error message string for most recent error on db, or NULL in rare cases of invalid UTF.
requirements: Pointer owned by SQLite; may be overwritten by later calls.

functions.name: sqlite3_errmsg16
functions.description: Returns a UTF-16 native-endian error message string. Same semantics as sqlite3_errmsg().
requirements: Managed by SQLite; do not free.

functions.name: sqlite3_errmsg16
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of sqlite3_errmsg.

functions.name: sqlite3_errstr
functions.description: Returns static English text for a given SQLite result code. Returns NULL if not available for the code.
requirements: Returned memory is static and must not be freed.

functions.name: sqlite3_errstr
functions.description: Return English text for a result code (UTF-8), or NULL if not available.
requirements: Pointer managed by SQLite; do not free.

functions.name: sqlite3_error_offset
functions.description: If the most recent error references a specific token in the SQL, returns the byte offset (UTF-8) of the token start; otherwise -1.
requirements: Examine immediately after failure to avoid being overwritten by other calls.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_errmsg
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_set_errmsg(sqlite3 *db, int errcode, const char *zErrMsg);
functions.description: Sets the error code and error message text for a database handle, overriding SQLite's own set values. Intended for extensions/wrappers.
requirements: db must be valid. errcode specifies result code. zErrMsg may be NULL to use default message for errcode.
Returns SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_NOMEM, or SQLITE_MISUSE.

functions.name: sqlite3_limit
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_limit(sqlite3*, int id, int newVal);
functions.description: Sets or queries connection-specific run-time limits (SQLITE_LIMIT_*). Returns the prior value regardless of change. Passing newVal<0 queries without changing.
requirements: id must be one of SQLITE_LIMIT_* constants.
Attempts above hard upper bound are silently truncated to the hard bound.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_prepare(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const char **pzTail);
functions.description: Legacy SQL statement compiler (UTF-8). Compiles the first statement in zSql into a prepared statement. Use sqlite3_prepare_v2/v3 for new code.
requirements: db must be valid; ppStmt non-NULL. zSql UTF-8; if nByte<0 read to nul, else max bytes.
*ppStmt set to NULL on error or if no SQL. *pzTail points to unused SQL after the first statement if non-NULL.
Must finalize ppStmt with sqlite3_finalize() when done.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_prepare_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const char **pzTail);
functions.description: Preferred SQL compiler (UTF-8). Returns detailed error codes directly from sqlite3_step(), auto-reprepares on schema changes and for certain bound-parameter influences.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_prepare() lifecycle.
Reprepare may occur during sqlite3_step(); keep authorizer/progress/trace consistent across step() calls.
Finalize statements when done.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare_v3
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_prepare_v3(sqlite3 *db, const char *zSql, int nByte, unsigned int prepFlags, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const char **pzTail);
functions.description: Like sqlite3_prepare_v2() with additional prepFlags (OR of SQLITE_PREPARE_*).
requirements: prepFlags may include SQLITE_PREPARE_PERSISTENT/NO_VTAB/DONT_LOG.
Other requirements as sqlite3_prepare_v2().

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_prepare16(sqlite3 *db, const void *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const void **pzTail);
functions.description: Legacy UTF-16 compiler. Use sqlite3_prepare16_v2/v3 for new code.
requirements: zSql must be UTF-16 native-endian. Other lifecycle as sqlite3_prepare().

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare16_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_prepare16_v2(sqlite3 *db, const void *zSql, int nByte, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const void **pzTail);
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of sqlite3_prepare_v2().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_prepare_v2() with UTF-16 input.

functions.name: sqlite3_prepare16_v3
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_prepare16_v3(sqlite3 *db, const void *zSql, int nByte, unsigned int prepFlags, sqlite3_stmt **ppStmt, const void **pzTail);
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of sqlite3_prepare_v3().
requirements: Same as sqlite3_prepare_v3() with UTF-16 input.

functions.name: sqlite3_sql
functions.description: Returns the original UTF-8 SQL text used to create the prepared statement (v2/v3/16_v2/16_v3), or NULL for legacy prepare().
requirements: Do not free the returned pointer; valid until statement finalized.

functions.name: sqlite3_expanded_sql
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated UTF-8 string of the SQL for the prepared statement with bound parameters expanded (values substituted).
requirements: May return NULL on OOM or if size exceeds SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH. Caller must sqlite3_free() the returned string.
Expansion length may be limited at compile time (SQLITE_TRACE_SIZE_LIMIT).

functions.name: sqlite3_normalized_sql
functions.description: Returns a normalized SQL string for the prepared statement (literal values replaced with placeholders). Available only if built with SQLITE_ENABLE_NORMALIZE.
requirements: Do not free the returned pointer; valid until statement finalized.
Only available when compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_NORMALIZE.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_readonly
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the prepared statement does not directly change database content (read-only).
requirements: Statement must be valid and not finalized.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_isexplain
functions.description: Returns 1 if statement is EXPLAIN, 2 if EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, or 0 otherwise.
requirements: Statement must be valid and not finalized.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_explain
functions.description: Switches the EXPLAIN mode of a prepared statement at runtime: 0 normal, 1 EXPLAIN, 2 EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. May trigger reprepare. Fails if created with legacy prepare().
requirements: Call sqlite3_reset(pStmt) before changing explain mode.
Affects statement behavior but not sqlite3_sql() text.

functions.name: sqlite3_stmt_busy
functions.description: Returns non-zero if sqlite3_step() has been called and neither SQLITE_DONE returned nor sqlite3_reset() called since (i.e., the statement is "busy").
requirements: Statement must be valid and not finalized.

functions.name: sqlite3_data_count
functions.description: Returns the number of columns in the current row if sqlite3_step() returned SQLITE_ROW and not yet reset/done. Returns 0 otherwise.
requirements: Call only after sqlite3_step() returned SQLITE_ROW to get the count.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_blob
functions.description: Returns pointer to BLOB data for column iCol of current row. Valid until next type conversion, sqlite3_step(), sqlite3_reset(), or finalize. Zero-length BLOB yields NULL pointer.
requirements: Must be called only when sqlite3_step() returned SQLITE_ROW and before reset/finalize.
iCol in range 0..column_count-1.
Do not free returned pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_double
functions.description: Returns column value as double, performing conversions as documented.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_int
functions.description: Returns column value as 32-bit int, with documented conversion semantics.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_int64
functions.description: Returns column value as 64-bit integer.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_text
functions.signature: SQLITE_API const unsigned char *sqlite3_column_text(sqlite3_stmt*, int iCol);
functions.description: Returns UTF-8 text for column iCol of current row; zero-terminated. Pointer may be invalidated by subsequent conversions or step/reset/finalize.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range. Do not free pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_text16
functions.description: Returns UTF-16 native-endian text for column iCol of current row; zero-terminated.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_value
functions.description: Returns an unprotected sqlite3_value object for column iCol. Useful primarily within SQL function/vtable context. Only safe for sqlite3_bind_value()/sqlite3_result_value().
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.
Unprotected value is not threadsafe for general use.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_bytes
functions.description: Returns size in bytes of BLOB or UTF-8 TEXT column; for UTF-16 text, converts to UTF-8 first. For numeric types, returns bytes of their text representation. For NULL returns 0.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.
Call after retrieving text/blob to force the desired encoding first for stable size.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_bytes16
functions.description: Returns size in bytes of BLOB or UTF-16 TEXT column; for UTF-8 text converts to UTF-16 first. Numeric types converted to UTF-16 text.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_type
functions.description: Returns the initial datatype code (SQLITE_INTEGER/FLOAT/TEXT/BLOB/NULL) of column iCol before any conversion. After conversion, value may be undefined.
requirements: Statement must be on a row; iCol in range.

functions.name: sqlite3_finalize
functions.description: Destroys a prepared statement object, freeing resources. Returns SQLITE_OK if the most recent evaluation had no errors; otherwise an error code may be returned.
requirements: It is an error to use a prepared statement after finalizing.
May be called at any point in the statement lifecycle. Passing NULL is a harmless no-op.

functions.name: sqlite3_finalize
functions.description: Delete a prepared statement object, releasing resources. Returns SQLITE_OK if last evaluation had no error, otherwise last error code.
requirements: Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
After finalize, stmt pointer must not be used.

functions.name: sqlite3_reset
functions.description: Resets a prepared statement back to its initial state ready for re-execution. Does not clear parameter bindings.
requirements: Check the return code to detect prior step() errors or errors during reset itself.
Use sqlite3_clear_bindings() to clear bound values.

functions.name: sqlite3_reset
functions.description: Reset a prepared statement to run again, retaining bindings. Returns last step() status (OK if never stepped) or error if reset encounters one.
requirements: Bindings are preserved; use sqlite3_clear_bindings to clear.
Check return even if previous step() was OK.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_function
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_function(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*));
functions.description: Register or redefine a scalar or aggregate SQL function on database connection db. For scalar provide xFunc only; for aggregate provide xStep and xFinal. eTextRep encodes preferred text encoding and optional flags (e.g., SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC).
requirements: db must be a valid open sqlite3*.
zFunctionName UTF-8 name length ≤ 255 bytes (excluding NUL).
nArg: -1 for variable arity, 0..127 fixed; other values undefined.
eTextRep must be one of SQLITE_UTF8/UTF16* optionally ORed with flags (e.g., SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC, SQLITE_DIRECTONLY, SQLITE_INNOCUOUS, SQLITE_SUBTYPE, SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE).
If registering aggregate, xStep and xFinal non-NULL; scalar: xFunc non-NULL; deleting a function: pass all three callback pointers NULL.
Callbacks must not close or reset the invoking statement/db; must be threadsafe per SQLite rules.
Returns SQLITE_OK on success; error code otherwise.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_function16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_function16(sqlite3 *db, const void *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*));
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of sqlite3_create_function; zFunctionName is UTF-16 in native byte order.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_create_function, but zFunctionName is UTF-16 native-endian NUL-terminated.
Follow same rules for nArg/eTextRep/callbacks.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_function_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_function_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xFunc)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*), void (*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Like sqlite3_create_function with an extra destructor xDestroy for pApp, called when the function is dropped or registration fails.
requirements: All requirements of sqlite3_create_function apply.
xDestroy may be NULL; if non-NULL it is called once when function is deleted or on registration failure.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_window_function
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_window_function(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFunctionName, int nArg, int eTextRep, void *pApp, void (*xStep)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xFinal)(sqlite3_context*), void (*xValue)(sqlite3_context*), void (*xInverse)(sqlite3_context*,int,sqlite3_value**), void (*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Register or redefine an aggregate window function on db. Provide xStep/xFinal, and optionally xValue/xInverse to support window frames.
requirements: db must be valid.
zFunctionName UTF-8 name ≤ 255 bytes.
nArg -1 or 0..127.
eTextRep encoding/flags as documented.
xStep and xFinal must be non-NULL. If xValue/xInverse are both NULL, function is a regular aggregate; otherwise it can be used as window function too.
xDestroy may be NULL; called to free pApp.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_blob
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_blob(sqlite3_context *ctx, const void *v, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Set the SQL function result to a BLOB of n bytes from v. xDel controls lifetime (SQLITE_TRANSIENT, SQLITE_STATIC, or destructor).
requirements: Must be called within a SQL function context callback.
If n<0 behavior undefined; pass actual byte count.
If xDel is SQLITE_TRANSIENT, SQLite copies data; SQLITE_STATIC means buffer remains valid until function returns; otherwise xDel(v) will be called when SQLite finishes with it.
Do not use after ctx finishes.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_blob64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_blob64(sqlite3_context *ctx, const void *v, sqlite3_uint64 n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: 64-bit length variant of sqlite3_result_blob.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_result_blob; n is 64-bit length.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_double
functions.description: Set the SQL function result to a floating-point value v.
requirements: Call only within function context.
If built without floating point, double may be typedef to integer as per build options.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_error(sqlite3_context *ctx, const char *z, int n);
functions.description: Cause function to throw an error with UTF-8 message z (length n or up to NUL if n<0).
requirements: Call from SQL function context.
If n>=0, it is byte count; if n<0, uses up to first NUL.
SQLite copies message; caller can free z after return.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_error16(sqlite3_context *ctx, const void *z, int n);
functions.description: Like sqlite3_result_error but message z is UTF-16 native-endian.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_result_error; byte-order rules per docs (BOM handling).

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error_toobig
functions.description: Throw an SQLITE_TOOBIG error for the current function.
requirements: Call within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error_nomem
functions.description: Throw an SQLITE_NOMEM error for the current function.
requirements: Call within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_error_code
functions.description: Set specific error code errcode for the current function error state (default is SQLITE_ERROR).
requirements: Must be called after signaling an error via sqlite3_result_error* to override code, or to set code before returning error.
Use only within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_int
functions.description: Set SQL function result to 32-bit integer v.
requirements: Use within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_int64
functions.description: Set SQL function result to 64-bit integer v.
requirements: Use within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_null
functions.description: Set SQL function result to NULL.
requirements: Use within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text(sqlite3_context *ctx, const char *z, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Set SQL function result to a UTF-8 text string of n bytes (excluding NUL). xDel controls lifetime (TRANSIENT/STATIC/destructor).
requirements: If n<0, SQLite computes length up to first NUL; if n>=0, may include embedded NULs.
xDel semantics same as blob variant.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text64(sqlite3_context *ctx, const char *z, sqlite3_uint64 n, void (*xDel)(void*), unsigned char encoding);
functions.description: Set SQL function result to text of n bytes with specified encoding indicator (SQLITE_UTF8/SQLITE_UTF16/BE/LE).
requirements: encoding must be one of documented values.
Other semantics same as sqlite3_result_text.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text16(sqlite3_context *ctx, const void *z, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Set result to UTF-16 native-endian text string.
requirements: Byte-order rules apply with BOM handling; n semantics as above.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16le
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text16le(sqlite3_context *ctx, const void *z, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Set result to UTF-16 little-endian text.
requirements: Same as text16; BOM handling per docs.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_text16be
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_text16be(sqlite3_context *ctx, const void *z, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Set result to UTF-16 big-endian text.
requirements: Same as text16; BOM handling per docs.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_value
functions.description: Set function result to a copy of sqlite3_value v (protected or unprotected).
requirements: SQLite copies value; v may be freed after return.
Use only within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_pointer
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_pointer(sqlite3_context *ctx, void *p, const char *zPType, void (*xDestructor)(void*));
functions.description: Set function result to a typed pointer (NULL SQL value with associated pointer p and type string zPType). Use with sqlite3_value_pointer to retrieve.
requirements: zPType should be a static string literal identifying the pointer type.
xDestructor called with p when SQLite no longer needs it; may be NULL.
Use only within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_zeroblob
functions.description: Set result to a zero-filled BLOB of n bytes (32-bit length). Efficient placeholder for later incremental I/O.
requirements: n must be >=0; negative results in zero-length BLOB.
Use within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_zeroblob64
functions.description: Set result to zero-filled BLOB of n bytes (64-bit). Returns SQLITE_OK or error code.
requirements: Use within function context.
n can be large; if too large for limits, returns error.

functions.name: sqlite3_result_subtype
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_result_subtype(sqlite3_context *ctx, unsigned int T);
functions.description: Associate an application-defined subtype (low 8 bits preserved) with the current function result.
requirements: Should be used only by functions registered with SQLITE_RESULT_SUBTYPE property; otherwise might be ignored or error in strict builds.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_blob
functions.description: Return a pointer to the BLOB content of value v. May be invalidated by subsequent conversions. Returns NULL if v is NULL or OOM conversion triggers.
requirements: v must be a valid sqlite3_value* (protected for use in value_* family).
Do not free returned pointer; valid until next type conversion or statement step/reset/finalize.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_double
functions.description: Return v as a double, with conversion if needed. On OOM conversion, returns 0 and error can be checked via sqlite3_errcode().
requirements: v must be a valid sqlite3_value*.
Thread-safety note for unprotected values: only safe from within function/virtual table contexts.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_int
functions.description: Return v as 32-bit integer, with conversion if needed.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_int64
functions.description: Return v as 64-bit integer, with conversion if needed.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_pointer
functions.description: Retrieve a typed pointer previously stored via sqlite3_result_pointer, if type string matches zPType. Returns NULL if types differ or v not a pointer.
requirements: zPType must match the original type string (strcmp).
Use only on values that originated from sqlite3_result_pointer.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text
functions.description: Return UTF-8 text representation of v, performing conversion if necessary. Returns NULL on NULL or OOM.
requirements: Result may be invalidated by further conversions or API calls on same value/context.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text16
functions.description: Return UTF-16 native-endian text representation of v.
requirements: Same invalidation rules as other value accessors.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text16le
functions.description: Return UTF-16 little-endian text representation of v.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_text16be
functions.description: Return UTF-16 big-endian text representation of v.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_bytes
functions.description: Return size in bytes of BLOB or UTF-8 text content of v (without NUL terminator). If text in other encoding, converts to UTF-8 to count.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_bytes16
functions.description: Return size in bytes of UTF-16 content of v; converts if needed.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_type
functions.description: Return one of SQLITE_INTEGER/SQLITE_FLOAT/SQLITE_TEXT/SQLITE_BLOB/SQLITE_NULL for the current type prior to any conversion.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_numeric_type
functions.description: Apply numeric affinity if possible and return numeric type code (INTEGER or FLOAT) or original type if not convertible.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_nochange
functions.description: Within a virtual table xUpdate, returns non-zero if this value is a no-change placeholder for an unmodified column (via sqlite3_vtab_nochange/xColumn optimization).
requirements: Only meaningful within xUpdate of virtual tables. Outside of that, return value is arbitrary.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_frombind
functions.description: Return non-zero if value v originated from a bound parameter, zero otherwise.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_dup
functions.description: Create a protected copy of sqlite3_value v. Returns NULL on OOM or if v is NULL.
requirements: If v is a pointer value, result is a NULL SQL value per docs.

functions.name: sqlite3_value_free
functions.description: Free a value obtained from sqlite3_value_dup().
requirements: Safe to pass NULL (no-op).
Do not free values not obtained from sqlite3_value_dup().

functions.name: sqlite3_value_encoding
functions.description: Report current text encoding of v (SQLITE_UTF8/SQLITE_UTF16BE/SQLITE_UTF16LE) if v is TEXT. Otherwise return value meaningless.
requirements: Intended for testing/validation; avoid use in normal apps.

functions.name: sqlite3_aggregate_context
functions.description: Obtain per-aggregate-call state buffer of nBytes, zero-initialized on first call. Returns same pointer on subsequent calls; may return NULL on OOM or if nBytes<=0 on first call.
requirements: Call only within aggregate xStep/xFinal callbacks.
nBytes should be >0 on first call to allocate; pass 0 in xFinal to avoid allocation.

functions.name: sqlite3_user_data
functions.description: Return pApp pointer registered with sqlite3_create_function* for the current function context.
requirements: Use only within function/window callbacks.

functions.name: sqlite3_context_db_handle
functions.description: Return database connection handle associated with current function context.
requirements: Use only within function context.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_auxdata
functions.description: Retrieve function auxiliary data previously set via sqlite3_set_auxdata for argument N of current function invocation. Returns NULL if none.
requirements: Only valid within current function call; do not free returned pointer unless you own it.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_auxdata
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void sqlite3_set_auxdata(sqlite3_context *ctx, int N, void *p, void (*xDelete)(void*));
functions.description: Associate aux data pointer p with argument N of current function; SQLite will call xDelete(p) once when it discards it (or immediately on OOM/plan-time evaluation).
requirements: xDelete may be NULL; then SQLite will not free p.
Should be called near end of function to avoid immediate destructor calls in planning scenarios.
Aux data may be discarded at various times as documented.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_clientdata
functions.description: Fetch a pointer associated with database connection db under name N, previously set via sqlite3_set_clientdata.
requirements: N compared by strcmp; case-sensitive.
Returns NULL if not set.
Do not free returned pointer unless you control its lifetime.

functions.name: sqlite3_set_clientdata
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_set_clientdata(sqlite3 *db, const char *N, void *P, void (*X)(void*));
functions.description: Associate pointer P with database connection db using name N. If existing value present, its destructor X (old) is invoked. Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_NOMEM.
requirements: If P and X non-NULL and OOM occurs, X(P) is invoked.
Destructors for all clientdata are called exactly once when db closes or on replacement.
Names must be unique per connection; intended for wrappers; avoid exposing to untrusted code.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_blob
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_blob(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, const void *data, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Bind parameter idx (1-based) to a BLOB of n bytes from data. xDel controls lifetime (STATIC/TRANSIENT/destructor).
requirements: stmt must be a valid prepared statement and not finalized.
idx must be between 1 and bind count; else SQLITE_RANGE.
If stmt has been stepped and not reset, SQLITE_MISUSE.
xDel semantics same as result_blob.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_blob64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_blob64(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, const void *data, sqlite3_uint64 n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: 64-bit size variant of sqlite3_bind_blob.
requirements: Same as sqlite3_bind_blob.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_double
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_double(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, double v);
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to floating-point value v.
requirements: See sqlite3_bind_blob for general binding rules.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_int
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_int(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, int v);
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to 32-bit integer v.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_int64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_int64(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, sqlite3_int64 v);
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to 64-bit integer v.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_null
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to SQL NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_text
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_text(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, const char *z, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to UTF-8 text z of n bytes (or up to NUL if n<0). xDel controls lifetime.
requirements: If n>=0 may include embedded NULs; xDel semantics as above.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_text16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_text16(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, const void *z, int n, void (*xDel)(void*));
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to UTF-16 native-endian text.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_text64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_text64(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, const char *z, sqlite3_uint64 n, void (*xDel)(void*), unsigned char encoding);
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to text with explicit encoding flag (SQLITE_UTF8/UTF16/...).
requirements: encoding must be a valid value; undefined behavior otherwise.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_value
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_value(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, const sqlite3_value *v);
functions.description: Bind parameter idx to a copy of sqlite3_value v (type preserved).
requirements: v may be unprotected; SQLite copies value.
Binding a pointer value binds SQL NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_pointer
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_pointer(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, void *p, const char *zPType, void (*xDestructor)(void*));
functions.description: Bind idx to a typed pointer p with type string zPType. The SQL parameter reads as NULL but pointer retrievable in extensions via sqlite3_value_pointer.
requirements: zPType should be static/literal; xDestructor called when SQLite no longer needs p.
Returns SQLITE_OK or error.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_zeroblob
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_zeroblob(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, int n);
functions.description: Bind idx to a zero-filled BLOB of n bytes (placeholder).
requirements: Useful for incremental blob I/O.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_zeroblob64
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_bind_zeroblob64(sqlite3_stmt *stmt, int idx, sqlite3_uint64 n);
functions.description: 64-bit length variant of zeroblob bind.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_parameter_count
functions.description: Return the number of SQL parameters in prepared statement stmt.
requirements: stmt must be valid; returns 0 if none.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_parameter_name
functions.description: Return the name (including prefix) of parameter N (1-based) or NULL if unnamed/out of range.

functions.name: sqlite3_bind_parameter_index
functions.description: Return the index (1-based) of named parameter zName, or 0 if not found.

functions.name: sqlite3_clear_bindings
functions.description: Reset all bound parameters to NULL without resetting the statement.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_count
functions.description: Return number of columns in the result set for prepared statement pStmt.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_name
functions.description: Return UTF-8 name of result column N, or NULL on OOM. Valid until next sqlite3_step()/reset/finalize or next name call.
requirements: N is zero-based and must be < column count.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_name16
functions.description: Return UTF-16 native-endian name of result column N.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_database_name
functions.description: Return UTF-8 name of database for column N (requires SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA).
requirements: May return NULL if disabled or OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_database_name16
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of column database name.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_table_name
functions.description: Return UTF-8 table name for column N (requires SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA).

functions.name: sqlite3_column_table_name16
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of column table name.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_origin_name
functions.description: Return UTF-8 original un-aliased column name for result column N (requires SQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA).

functions.name: sqlite3_column_origin_name16
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of origin column name.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_decltype
functions.description: Return declared type string (UTF-8) of table column underlying result column N, or NULL if expression/subquery or OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_column_decltype16
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of column declared type.

functions.name: sqlite3_step
functions.description: Evaluate a prepared statement one step. Returns SQLITE_ROW (row available), SQLITE_DONE (finished), SQLITE_BUSY/ERROR/etc. as per docs.
requirements: stmt must be prepared and not finalized.
After SQLITE_ROW, use sqlite3_column_* to fetch values.
After error other than BUSY/MISUSE, legacy requires reset to get extended code; v2 prepares return extended code directly.
Behavior with no reset after non-ROW historically fixed to auto-reset since 3.6.23.1 unless SQLITE_OMIT_AUTORESET.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_collation
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_collation(sqlite3 *db, const char *zName, int eTextRep, void *pArg, int (*xCompare)(void*,int,const void*,int,const void*));
functions.description: Create or redefine collation named zName with comparator xCompare for specified eTextRep encoding on db.
requirements: db valid; zName UTF-8 unique per connection.
eTextRep one of SQLITE_UTF8/UTF16/LE/BE/ALIGNED.
xCompare must impose total ordering and be consistent across encodings if multiple registered.
To delete collation: pass xCompare NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_collation_v2
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_collation_v2(sqlite3 *db, const char *zName, int eTextRep, void *pArg, int (*xCompare)(void*,int,const void*,int,const void*), void (*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Like sqlite3_create_collation with an xDestroy callback for pArg when collation is dropped or replaced.
requirements: xDestroy not called if create_collation_v2 fails; caller must free in that case.

functions.name: sqlite3_create_collation16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_create_collation16(sqlite3 *db, const void *zName, int eTextRep, void *pArg, int (*xCompare)(void*,int,const void*,int,const void*));
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of sqlite3_create_collation; zName is UTF-16 native-endian.

functions.name: sqlite3_collation_needed
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_collation_needed(sqlite3 *db, void *pArg, void (*xCollNeeded)(void*,sqlite3*,int eTextRep,const char*));
functions.description: Register callback to be invoked when an undefined collation is required by compilation; name passed in UTF-8.
requirements: xCollNeeded may be NULL to disable.
Callback should register the needed collation.

functions.name: sqlite3_collation_needed16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_collation_needed16(sqlite3 *db, void *pArg, void (*xCollNeeded)(void*,sqlite3*,int eTextRep,const void*));
functions.description: UTF-16 variant of sqlite3_collation_needed; collation name passed in UTF-16 native-endian.

functions.name: sqlite3_sleep
functions.description: Suspend current thread for at least ms milliseconds (rounded by VFS). Returns actual requested milliseconds passed to OS (may be rounded).
requirements: Negative ms treated as 0 in newer versions; behavior depends on VFS per docs.

functions.name: sqlite3_temp_directory
functions.description: Global variable: directory path for temporary files for built-in VFS if set. Deprecated; avoid except on WinRT where required.
requirements: Not thread-safe to modify concurrently with DB use.
If modified directly, either set to NULL or an sqlite3_malloc-allocated buffer to be compatible with PRAGMA temp_store_directory.

functions.name: sqlite3_data_directory
functions.description: Windows-only global variable: base directory for relative DB filenames for built-in Windows VFS. Deprecated; modify only at process init.
requirements: Not thread-safe to modify concurrently.
Should be sqlite3_malloc-allocated if used with PRAGMA data_store_directory.

functions.name: sqlite3_win32_set_directory
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_win32_set_directory(unsigned long type, void *zValue);
functions.description: Windows-specific: set sqlite3_data_directory or sqlite3_temp_directory (type SQLITE_WIN32_DATA_DIRECTORY_TYPE or SQLITE_WIN32_TEMP_DIRECTORY_TYPE). zValue is UTF-16 or ANSI? This API takes void*, see win32_set_directory8/16 for typed versions.
requirements: Use the 8/16 variants for specific encodings.
Returns SQLITE_OK/SQLITE_ERROR/SQLITE_NOMEM.

functions.name: sqlite3_win32_set_directory8
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_win32_set_directory8(unsigned long type, const char *zValue);
functions.description: Windows: set directory using UTF-8 string.
requirements: type must be SQLITE_WIN32_DATA_DIRECTORY_TYPE or SQLITE_WIN32_TEMP_DIRECTORY_TYPE.

functions.name: sqlite3_win32_set_directory16
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_win32_set_directory16(unsigned long type, const void *zValue);
functions.description: Windows: set directory using UTF-16 string.
requirements: type must be SQLITE_WIN32_DATA_DIRECTORY_TYPE or SQLITE_WIN32_TEMP_DIRECTORY_TYPE.

functions.name: sqlite3_get_autocommit
functions.description: Return non-zero if db is in autocommit mode, zero otherwise.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_handle
functions.description: Return the database connection that owns prepared statement stmt.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_name
functions.description: Return schema name (e.g., "main", "temp" or attached name) for N-th database on connection db, or NULL if out of range.
requirements: String owned by SQLite, may be invalidated by schema changes.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_filename
functions.description: Return absolute filename for database zDbName on connection db, or NULL/empty for in-memory/temporary db.
requirements: Return may be used with sqlite3_uri_* helpers.

functions.name: sqlite3_db_readonly
functions.description: Return 1 if database zDbName is read-only, 0 if read-write, or -1 if name not a database on connection.

functions.name: sqlite3_txn_state
functions.description: Return transaction state of schema zSchema on connection db: SQLITE_TXN_NONE/READ/WRITE, or -1 if invalid schema name.

functions.name: sqlite3_next_stmt
functions.description: Iterate over all prepared statements on connection pDb. Pass pStmt=NULL to get first; otherwise get next; returns NULL if none.
requirements: pDb must be open.
Do not modify statements while iterating except to reset/finalize as intended.

functions.name: sqlite3_commit_hook
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when a transaction is committed on db. If callback returns non-zero, the commit is converted to a rollback. Returns previous pArg.
requirements: Callback must not modify the db connection (not reentrant).
Only one per connection; replaces previous.

functions.name: sqlite3_rollback_hook
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when a transaction is rolled back on db. Returns previous pArg.
requirements: Not reentrant; do not modify the same connection in callback.

functions.name: sqlite3_autovacuum_pages
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_autovacuum_pages(sqlite3 *db, unsigned int(*xCallback)(void*,const char*,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int), void *pArg, void (*xDestroy)(void*));
functions.description: Register an auto-vacuum pages callback to control/predict autovacuum compaction for database schemas. Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_MISUSE.
requirements: Callback must be non-reentrant and simple (no SQLite APIs).
xDestroy called on pArg when replaced or db close. Only one per connection.

functions.name: sqlite3_update_hook
functions.signature: SQLITE_API void *sqlite3_update_hook(sqlite3 *db, void (*xCallback)(void*,int,const char*,const char*,sqlite3_int64), void *pArg);
functions.description: Register a callback invoked on each row change to rowid tables (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). Returns previous pArg.
requirements: Callback must not modify the same connection while executing.
Not invoked for WITHOUT ROWID and internal tables; behavior noted for REPLACE, truncate optimization.

functions.name: sqlite3_enable_shared_cache
functions.description: Enable or disable process-wide shared pager cache mode. Use discouraged. Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_MISUSE on some platforms.
requirements: Call before opening connections; process-global setting; not supported on some platforms (macOS/iOS returns MISUSE).

functions.name: sqlite3_release_memory
functions.description: Attempt to free up to N bytes of heap memory from non-essential internal caches. Returns actual bytes freed (0 if disabled).

functions.name: sqlite3_db_release_memory
functions.description: Attempt to free as much memory as possible from per-connection caches for db. Returns SQLITE_OK.

functions.name: sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64
functions.description: Set or query global soft heap limit in bytes. Returns previous limit (or current if N<0). 0 disables limiter.
requirements: Soft limit ≤ hard limit; subject to build-time/memstatus conditions.

functions.name: sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64
functions.description: Set or query global hard heap limit in bytes. Allocations fail when exceeded. Returns previous (or current if N<0). 0 disables.
requirements: Adjusts soft limit if necessary.

functions.name: sqlite3_soft_heap_limit
functions.description: Deprecated 32-bit variant of sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64.
requirements: Use sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64 instead.

functions.name: sqlite3_table_column_metadata
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_table_column_metadata(sqlite3 *db, const char *zDbName, const char *zTableName, const char *zColumnName, char const **pzDataType, char const **pzCollSeq, int *pNotNull, int *pPrimaryKey, int *pAutoinc);
functions.description: Return metadata about a column of a table: declared type, collation, NOT NULL, PK, AUTOINCREMENT. Returns SQLITE_OK or error.
requirements: db must be open.
zDbName may be NULL to search attached DBs.
zTableName must not be NULL; zColumnName may be NULL to just check table existence.
Writes outputs only when successful.

functions.name: sqlite3_load_extension
functions.signature: SQLITE_API int sqlite3_load_extension(sqlite3 *db, const char *zFile, const char *zProc, char **pzErrMsg);
functions.description: Load a shared library extension zFile and optionally entry point zProc (or derive). Returns SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_ERROR and error message in *pzErrMsg (malloced) if provided. Requires extension loading be enabled.
requirements: Must enable via sqlite3_enable_load_extension or sqlite3_db_config(SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION,1).
Caller must sqlite3_free(*pzErrMsg) on error.
Not secure to expose to SQL unless needed.

functions.name: sqlite3_enable_load_extension
functions.description: Enable or disable C-API load_extension() and SQL load_extension() for db. Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: Recommended to use SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION instead to keep SQL function disabled for security.

functions.name: sqlite3_auto_extension
functions.description: Register a statically-linked extension entry-point xEntryPoint to be automatically invoked for each new connection. Returns SQLITE_OK.
requirements: xEntryPoint signature: int (sqlite3*,char **,const sqlite3_api_routines*), but registered via shim that takes void(*)().
Calling with same pointer multiple times is a no-op.

functions.name: sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension
functions.description: Unregister a previously registered auto-extension entry-point. Returns 1 if removed, 0 if not found.

functions.name: sqlite3_reset_auto_extension
functions.description: Remove all registered auto-extensions.

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_alloc
functions.description: Allocate a mutex object. Argument is SQLITE_MUTEX_FAST/RECURSIVE or STATIC_* to retrieve a static mutex.
requirements: Do not free static mutexes.
Returns NULL on OOM.

functions.name: sqlite3_mutex_free
functions.description: Free a dynamic mutex allocated by sqlite3_mutex_alloc. Undefined behavior for static mutexes or NULL.
requirements: Only free dynamic (FAST/RECURSIVE) mutexes.
